sentences.text: 2 4. The entire trial is completed and also the petitioner/accused is examined under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. and the matter is posted for arguments.
At that stage the accused was absent and also there was no representation for the accused.
Hence, the learned Sessions Judge has issued non bailable warrant.
This is under challenge in this petition.

5. Learned counsel for petitioner submitted that the petitioner was present on all the dates throughout the proceedings and only on 29.01.2026 the accused was absent due to his inevitable personal work and the advocate was also absent due to his ill health.
Therefore, considering that the accused was absent and there was no representation, the Special Court has issued non bailable warrant against the petitioner/accused.
It is further submitted that the victim has turned hostile and nothing NC: 2026:KHC-D:3599 HC-KAR has been stated against the accused.
It is further submitted that both the victim and the petitioner/accused have got married and produced the marriage certificate.

Therefore submitted that the petitioner is under threat of arrest by the police and hence prays to give one more chance to appear before the Special Court and co-operate for early disposal of the case.

6. Considering the material annexed to the petition, it is seen that the victim is examined as PW.1 and has turned hostile and she has stated nothing incriminating circumstances against the petitioner/accused.
Further, in the evidence it is stated that PW.1 has married the accused.
But now due to issuance of non bailable warrant and also cancelling the bail, the petitioner is under the apprehension of arrest.
The petitioner has filed petition with a prayer to attend the Court regularly and co-operate for early disposal of the case.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3599 HC-KAR 7.

Considering the above discussions and reasons that now the victim has turned hostile and as per the marriage certificate produced along with the petition, both the victim and the petitioner/accused have married and therefore to give one chance to appear before the Court, the order of the Sessions Court is to be set aside with a direction to the petitioner/accused to appear before the Sessions Court and co-operate for early disposal of the case.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The petition is allowed.
ii) The order dated 29.01.2026 passed in Spl.Case No.256/2025, by the Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, Belagavi, is hereby set aside.
iii) The petitioner/accused is directed to appear before the Sessions Court and file application for bail.
